XSYNC USER MANUALSECTION 1

xs-snapshot(1) ​

Resume & snapshots

Resume verified partial data, reuse unchanged snapshot files, and control writes.

PARTIAL TRANSFERS ​

Retain partial data and show progress
sh
xs -aP src/ dst/

With --partial or -P, xsync verifies an existing destination prefix on both sides before reusing it. A matching prefix avoids sending the same bytes again; a mismatch sends the file in full. Retained interrupted output contains its completed contiguous prefix.

NOTE

Small files up to 512 KiB use the whole-file path. A protocol-3 peer has no verified-prefix resume feature and transfers the file in full.

DELTA AND WHOLE-FILE TRANSFERS ​

Allow verified reuse
sh
xs -aP --no-whole-file src/ dst/
Disable resume and block matching
sh
xs -aP --whole-file src/ dst/

Large changed local and remote files can reuse verified blocks from a readable existing destination. Eligible APFS clones remain preferred for local copies. -W disables resume and delta block matching.

SNAPSHOT REUSE ​

Reuse a previous snapshot
sh
xs -aP --link-dest=../previous/ src/ snapshots/current/

Relative --link-dest paths start at the destination directory. In this example, the basis is snapshots/previous/. Up to 20 previous snapshot directories may be supplied.

Unchanged files with matching requested metadata become hard links. Changed files, different requested metadata, or cross-device links create independent copies. A previous snapshot may also supply a read-only delta basis.

A dated snapshot that hard-links unchanged files
sh
xs -ai --link-dest=../2026-10-09 src/ snapshots/2026-10-10/
stat -c "%h links  %n" snapshots/2026-10-10/notes.txt snapshots/2026-10-10/docs/guide.md
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
created directory snapshots/2026-10-10
>f.st...... notes.txt
1 links  snapshots/2026-10-10/notes.txt
2 links  snapshots/2026-10-10/docs/guide.md

SHARED FILES ​

SNAPSHOTS

Hard-linked snapshots share the same inode. Later in-place writes or metadata changes to an already shared destination can affect other links. Create a new snapshot directory and keep old snapshots read-only by workflow.

ATOMIC AND IN-PLACE OUTPUT ​

New byte-copied files are atomic by default: xsync writes a temporary name and publishes it by rename after verification. --no-atomic writes new files directly; --inplace explicitly writes destination files in place.

State the default atomic policy explicitly
sh
xs -aP --atomic src/ dst/

Direct writing changes interruption behavior and can leave incomplete files under final names. Atomic staging and retained partials also need destination disk space.
